## What the chronicles say [Record]

Długosz's story: in late April 1434 Jogaila, riding to Gródek near Lviv, stood at night in the forest at [Medyka](../places/medyka.qmd) to hear the nightingales, took a cold in the frost, and weeks later died ([the death](ev_jogaila_dies.qmd)). The nightingale detail is a chronicler's anecdote; the chill is the stated cause.

## What really happened [Saga]

The saga keeps the nightingales and gives the king his silence: he stands in two cloaks at the forest edge while his chamberlains cough around him (Book V ch. 12). The last confession that follows is invention.

## Consequences

Leads to [Jogaila's death at Gródek](ev_jogaila_dies.qmd) on 1 June 1434.

## Dramatisation

Book V ch. 12 *Lakštingala* (Jogaila; late April 1434; Medyka).
